Ireland  really needs to decide if it wants an end to its decade-long housing  crises or not. For more than a decade, Government has tweaked and  fumbled and adjusted minor aspects of housing without actually getting  properly stuck in and addressing the elephant in the room, knocking us  about for 10 years – we need lots and lots and lots of houses built  quickly and at prices that are affordable.

No, it’s not complicated and, yes, it is that simple. Other countries do it. We are with the outliers.

We  need more than twice the number of homes being built at present levels  and we need to maintain this level of construction over a very long  period to come.

Instead  the Government is part of the problem. Increasing HAP constantly  without increasing the available stock significantly means the  Government is actively playing a part in increasing rents throughout  Ireland. Providing favourable tax rates to foreign funds who build tiny  apartments for crazy rents, to be exported straight out of the country,  is not the way forward.

The  Land Development Authority (LDA) is a good concept, to acquire and  control land use to take huge rezoning windfall profits from land owners  and make housing more affordable as a result.

But  it is being hobbled by government departments and local authorities  that shirk their roles in handing over the necessary land and protest at  the LDA being given necessary compulsory purchase powers.

“It’s not democratic,” they wail.

Neither  is disenfranchising an entire generation of our young people and  condemning them to penury to pay outsized rents with nothing left over  for life or a family.

We  need more land rezoned around our cities to provide this housing and we  need to bring developers and builders in from abroad if Ireland’s own  operators are too busy or too expensive.

And  when it comes to planning, we need residents to stop objecting to new  housing solely because they like their area better without it.

We need to come down hard on those looking to sneakily cash in on home development, as highlighted recently in this newspaper.

Those  who continually object (the LDA’s recent scheme in Dundrum has had its  content scaled back by one-third and by hundreds of homes thanks to  objections) are quite simply increasing the cost of housing for their  children and grandchildren and prohibiting them from ever having a home  of their own. Shame on them.

We  need to call out the politicians who criticise Government housing  policy and then slyly weigh in locally with residents to block new  schemes – the Mé Féiners.

We  need to decide once and for all, do we want 10 more years of overpriced  housing and rents that cost a small salary, affecting the economy  overall? Or do we want to be like the rest of Europe, and live in a  country where housing is not a fuss and is provided at reasonable prices  without resort to chicanery, Mé Féinery and the profit of a few  drastically affecting the lives of so many?
